extracted.intended_audience: recreational anglers, charter operators, state fish and wildlife agencies, fisheries managers, and members of the public who may submit comments on the rule
extracted.subtask_description: An inseason temporary rule implementing fishing dates, subarea openings/closures, and an allocation transfer for the 2025 Pacific halibut Area 2A recreational fishery, including procedural and legal bases for waiving prior notice and comment and for making the rule effective immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for inseason modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Pacific halibut regulations for Area 2A provide NMFS with the authority to make inseason modifications to recreational fishing periods and subarea allocations (50 CFR 300.63(c)(6)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such authority is exercised following consultation with the Council, IPHC, and the affected states; NMFS regulations allow the Regional Administrator to modify sport fishing periods, bag limits, size limits, days per calendar week, and subarea allocations inseason when the action supports annual allocation objectives and will not exceed the catch limit for a subarea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation objective constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Inseason modifications may be implemented to allow for allocation objectives to be met, as long as they do not result in exceeding the allocation for the area (50 CFR 300.63(c)(6)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NMFS must ensure actions increase opportunity or otherwise support meeting the overall Area 2A recreational fishery allocation without causing an area to exceed its catch limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Inseason modifications are taken following consultation with the Council, the International Pacific Halibut Commission (IPHC), and the affected states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule cites consultation with WDFW and ODFW and uses state-provided landings data (e.g., updated landings data provided July 15, 2025) as the factual basis for decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement and notification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 50 CFR 300.63(c), inseason actions are announced in the Federal Register and also on the NMFS hotline at (206) 526-6667 or (800) 662-9825.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NMFS will also notify anglers via a telephone hotline, news release, and by the relevant state Fish and Wildlife agencies; weekly catch reports are available on state Fish and Wildlife agency websites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and data basis for inseason actions
rubrics_metrics.description: NMFS will continue to monitor recreational catch estimates obtained via state sampling procedures until NMFS has determined that there is not sufficient subarea allocation for another full day of fishing or until there are no more open fishing dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions are based on state-supplied landings (pounds and metric tons) and percent remaining; example figures from June 30, 2025 are provided for each subarea to justify actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for reopening after June 30
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule (90 FR 14422) stated that, if sufficient subarea allocations remain for at least another full day of fishing after June 30, NMFS may take inseason action to reopen the Columbia River and Washington subareas in August, up to 7 days per week, through September.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pre-existing provision was part of the earlier rulemaking establishing 2025 fishing periods and is used here as the trigger for inseason reopening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation transfer practice and constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: NMFS may transfer allocation from one subarea to another to meet overall allocation objectives (example: transfer of 5,000 pounds from the Oregon Central Coast subarea to the Columbia River subarea).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers should be implemented so they do not reduce fishing opportunities in donor subareas and must still ensure no subarea exceeds its catch limit; the rule states the transfer is not anticipated to reduce Oregon opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good cause waiver for prior notice and comment (5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B), there is good cause to waive prior notice and an opportunity for public comment on this action, as notice and comment would be impracticable and contrary to the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NMFS explains the waiver reasoning: (a) conditions for inseason action were previously anticipated in the final rule (so the action is not unexpected), (b) timely action is necessary to meet allocation objectives and economic benefits, and (c) delay would undermine the benefit intended to fishery participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of 30-day delay in effective date (5 U.S.C. 553(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: NMFS finds good cause under 5 U.S.C. 553(d)(3) (and (d)(1)) to waive the 30-day delay in effective date and make the action effective on August 16, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: a delay would constrain fishing opportunity, be inconsistent with Catch Sharing Plan goals, potentially limit economic opportunity for fishing communities, and prevent necessary planning by stakeholders; absent the delay participants would otherwise be able to fish on the additional dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission requirements and public record
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments identified by NOAA-NMFS-2024-0139 via Regulations.gov or by mail to the provided address; comments must be received by the comment deadline (on or before August 26, 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NMFS may not consider comments sent by other methods or received after the comment period ends; all comments become part of the public record and will be posted on Regulations.gov without change; personal identifying information submitted voluntarily will be publicly accessible; anonymous comments accepted (enter 'N/A').

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates and area-specific inseason measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective August 16, 2025, through September 30, 2025 in the Washington and Columbia River subareas, and August 16, 2025, through October 31, 2025 in the Oregon Central Coast subarea; specific opening schedules by subarea are published (e.g., Puget Sound open 7 days/week Aug 16–Sep 30; North Coast open 7 days/week Aug 16–Sep 30; South Coast and Columbia River open Sunday–Friday on listed dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each subarea remains open only 'until there is not sufficient allocation for another full day of fishing and the area is therefore closed.' The Columbia River subarea also receives a specific allocation transfer of 5,000 pounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory and statutory citations for classification
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is issued pursuant to the Northern Pacific Halibut Act of 1982 and under regulatory authority at 50 CFR 300.63(c)(6); it is exempt from review under Executive Order 12866; authority: 16 U.S.C. 773-773k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule includes legal citations to justify issuance as a temporary inseason action and explains procedural statutory bases for waivers and immediate effectiveness (5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B), 553(d)(1)/(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to official document and supporting information
rubrics_metrics.description: The document is available as the official PDF on govinfo.gov and via the Federal Register website; background information and documents are available at the NOAA Fisheries action webpage and the Council's website; Regulations.gov docket provides comments and possibly supporting documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FederalRegister.gov provides XML renditions and links to the official PDF; the rule notes that supporting documents are available at stated sites (though 'No supporting documents available' is shown for this entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic and public interest considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The action is intended to provide opportunity for anglers and achieve the overall recreational fishery allocation to realize economic benefits to fishery participants and associated communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NMFS states timely implementation is necessary for business and personal planning by the regulated public, including recreational charter operations, port businesses, and private anglers who do not live near coastal access points; NMFS also states 'No aspect of this action is controversial.'
